decision: GO for isolated implementation of the revised ring-decoupling plan; no GPU or exact-source approval yet.
scope: Only COMP && CL == 1 SK2 templates. Keep all original escape warps, correction planes, launch geometry, shared allocation, and occupancy queries. Replace the escape warps' reads from staged x with the identical BF16 global x and remove only their full/empty ring participation. Empty barriers count regular NW consumer arrivals; final cbar still counts 32*NESC escape threads.
verified_design_facts: Source inspection confirms launch_sk2's tensor map and x pointer refer to the same contiguous BF16 input.
UV pooler input is the actual timed xuv buffer with M=2T; the prior output projection writes it, and the existing all-thread griddepcontrol.wait precedes correction work.
BND and FUSE transformations occur in epilogues; escape corrections use the original supplied input rows without applying those transformations themselves.
Assigning each sorted patch to its original stage-mod-NESC correction plane preserves per-plane addition order; retain the parent's final plane summation order.
required_exact_source_gates: All patch rows/columns must stay in their original valid input range and correction ownership, including empty and dense patch lists and padded token lanes.
Each escape warp zeros its existing plane and every lane arrives at cbar after completion, even if its token lane is padding.
The escape-table and correction buffers remain disjoint from ring storage reused by producers and epilogues.
Only escape ring arrivals are removed. Every regular consumer must still release every full or FUSE router stage with the existing count and lifetime.
Cluster variants and non-compressed/router precision paths remain unchanged.
No new CTA-wide barrier may be placed after producer or escape early returns.

CPU simulation covers sorted patch assignment, identical per-plane arithmetic sequence, address mapping, and barrier participation across active template geometries and M=1..32 including UV doubled rows.
performance_hazards: Global scalar input reads are strided across token lanes; two useful bytes can require a 32-byte cache sector. Extra L2 traffic and issue instructions may outweigh removed ring waits.
Independent escape work may finish late and move the bottleneck to the final correction barrier.
Unchanged source-level launch geometry does not prove identical compiled registers or scheduling.
This plan establishes a distinct testable mechanism, not evidence of a speedup.
discarded_plan: The earlier one-escape-warp / density-threshold / reduced-planes variant is not approved or implemented by this review. Root narrowed the experiment to ring decoupling only.
